text:
Mathew Barzal is back on Long Island. He played his first game of the season Saturday in Anaheim, picked up an assist in a 6-2 win, and called the road back from knee inflammation the "hardest journey of my life" in one headline this week. The Islanders are easing him in with limited minutes, and tonight is his first home game back.

He returns to a team whose record runs well ahead of its play. The Islanders have a plus-5 goal difference on chances that say minus-10.7, and they took just 44% of the expected goals (the quality of chances each side creates) across their last five games. Ilya Sorokin, in the starter's crease at the morning skate per NHL.com's Stefen Rosner, is the main reason the standings look fine: .915 and plus-9.4 goals saved above expected. The fun is up front. Matthew Schaefer has 13 points in his last ten, a five-game point streak and a power-play goal in his 100th game, and Simon Holmstrom has five goals during a four-game point streak, though our numbers flag him as due to cool. Jean-Gabriel Pageau (lower body) skated too; Peter DeBoer said "fingers crossed" when asked if he would be ready, per Rosner.

Columbus arrives winless in four, outscored 16-7, and the chances say a good part of that is real: 49% of the expected goals. Sean Monahan (upper body) is out until around Nov. 25 and Conor Garland is on injured reserve, week to week. The bright spot is in net. Cam Talbot gets the start on a heater, .930 and plus-6.2 goals saved above expected over his last five starts, after a minus-13.7 season last year. At 14 points, our simulations give the Blue Jackets an 8% playoff chance.

Our numbers see 3.08 expected goals for New York and 2.91 for Columbus. Our sleepers both wear Columbus colors: Mathieu Olivier, a third-liner one goal from 50 for his career whose shots have been dangerous lately, and Charlie Coyle, pointless in five on 4.2 expected goals but 58% for a point tonight.
headline: Barzal comes home to a team outrunning its numbers
